Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Based on the information you've provided, here's a breakdown of the situation and a realistic assessment of whether you would be able to spot the Moon with the naked eye:

---

### 🌕 **Moon's Position and Visibility:**

- **Altitude:** -51.919°  
  - This means the Moon is **well below the horizon** (below the horizon is anything with an altitude less than 0°).
- **Azimuth:** 275.986°  
  - This is in the **northwest direction**, but since the Moon is below the horizon, it's not visible.
- **Illumination:** 5.75%  
  - This is a **new moon phase**, where the Moon is mostly in shadow. It's very faint and difficult to see.
- **Distance:** ~364,757 km  
  - This is just a bit **more than the average distance** of the Moon from Earth (about 384,400 km), so it's not unusually close.
- **Angle from the Sun:** 27.675°  
  - This is a **new moon**, so the Moon is very close to the Sun in the sky (within a few degrees), which is why it's not visible at night.

---

### 🌞 **Sun's Position:**

- **Altitude:** -23.762°  
  - The Sun is **below the horizon** (just over 23° below), so it's not visible.
- **Azimuth:** 281.646°  
  - This is in the **northwest**, which is the direction of sunset in Perth at this time of year.

---

### 🌌 **Sky Conditions:**

- **Sky Brightness:** Night  
  - So the sky is dark, which is good for seeing faint objects.
- **Clear Sky:**  
  - No cloud cover, so no obstruction.
- **Your Vision:**  
  - You're an **ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight**, which is fine for spotting the Moon when it's above the horizon and not too faint.

---

### 📏 **Conclusion:**

**No, you would not be able to spot the Moon right now.**

- The Moon is **below the horizon**, so it's not visible to the naked eye.
- It's in the **new moon phase**, which means it's **not illuminated** and is **very faint**.
- Even though the sky is clear and dark, the Moon is **not above the horizon**, so it's not visible from Perth at this time.

---

### ✅ **When Will the Moon Be Visible?**

The Moon will be visible again when it's above the horizon and more illuminated. This typically happens:

- **1–2 days after the new moon** (when it's a waxing crescent).
- The Moon rises **around 7–8 PM** in Perth during summer (July), so it will be visible in the evening sky.

You might want to check an astronomy app or website (like [TimeandDate.com](https://www.timeanddate.com) or [In The Sky](https://inthesky.org)) for the **next time the Moon is above the horizon** and **illuminated enough** to see with the naked eye.

---
